pr_title: catalog/lease: reduce contention during lease acquistion.
pr_body:
This patch makes the following changes to help improve the performance of descriptor lease acquisition:

1. Adds a multi-threaded benchmark (AcquireLeaseConcurrent) for acquiring and releasing lease, so we can objectively measure improvements to the leasing fast path (i.e. when a lease is already cached).
2. Removes mutexes from common fields used for acquiring leases, such as the expiration, session ID, and reference count.
3. The WaitForInit check inside the lease manager can be expensive since select on a channel needs a mutex, so an atomic is introduced as a short circuit after initialization is complete.
4. The sqlliveness session mutable state only consists of an expiration, so we can replace this field with an atomic. This reduces contention for session based leasing, since multiple readers may need to check expirations concurrently.

With these changes we see the following improvement on the microbenchmark for leasing:

issue_context.title: catalog/lease: improve mutex contention in `(*lease.descriptorState).findForTimestamp`
issue_context.body:
See this thread: https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C0168LW5THS/p1736962042684289

In a test, this mutex showed a huge amount of wait time. Since this function is read-only, we should be able to use a RWMutex.

Note that the `desc.incRefCount` is not a read-only operation, but that function has its own mutex.

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/a177cd4db0b55fed266bec84ddc67c93534258d4/pkg/sql/catalog/lease/descriptor_state.go#L90-L123

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f86c45a-08c1-46c0-834d-add7e7243781)

Jira issue: CRDB-46528
comments: Adopting a RWLock inside this code path in the normal case seems detrimental with a 10% degradation in a simple benchmark. I'm going to drop GA-blocker from this, since I don't think its fully trivial. A simple conversion is running into: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/17973 and the cost of the RWMutex it self, which is generally slower.

Dang. In Pebble there are a few mutexes that we ended up sharding to avoid contention. Eg:
 https://github.com/cockroachdb/pebble/blob/d4b77cbbf24807baafeebeffe7d7cc402c9d3f6b/sstable/block/category_stats.go#L197-L207

But I bet this is a lot harder to shard, assuming we need full mutual exclusion during writes.

@jbowens I was able to reduce contention in a synthetic workload by having removing the mutex and having something similar to an RCU (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read-copy-update). That does give a healthy boost in a synthetic microbenchmark, but I'm not sure if it's worth the complexity.

Nice! My two cents is that it's probably worth it. Eventually we expect customers to use 128-vCPU nodes. The workload I tested as a simple kv100 point lookup workload and not particularly unique, and it appeared to be limited by the parallelism permitted by this mutex's critical section.
